results.title: . Is it a coincidence that the areas with rare earth in Myanmar are also conflict zones?
results.description:
.
Is it a coincidence that the areas with rare earth in Myanmar are also conflict zones?

In northern Myanmar’s Kachin State, near the Chinese border, rare earth deposits overlap with areas controlled by armed groups like the KIO.

After the KIO took control of the Chipwi–Pangwa area, China initially closed the border for rare earth-related imports and exports.

Rare earth mining in Myanmar has become closely tied to local conflicts. Armed groups use mining revenues to fund their operations, while China seeks stable access to these critical minerals. The result is a pattern where resource-rich border regions are also hotspots of fighting.
Source: @CrisisGroup by Richard Horsey, Thomas Kean, Carolin Graf and David Muchiri Kimotho
Visualisations and imagery by Claire Boccon-Gibod, Paul Franz, Ysé Angerer and Jorge Gutiérrez Lucena

results.title: Myanmar's first corporate HSK test center opened at Myanmar Wanbao Mining Copper Ltd.
results.description:
Myanmar's first corporate HSK test center opened at Myanmar Wanbao Mining Copper Ltd. A total of 106 employees of the Monywa Copper Mine Project sat the inaugural HSK exam.

Customized workplace Chinese language training, jointly developed with Shandong Polytechnic College, helped learners prepare for the test. Many earned excellent scores, including full marks.

It is another success story of the "Chinese +TVET" initiative — a story of empowering local talent and supporting China-Myanmar industrial cooperation.

#CLECInAction #HSK #ChinaMyanmarTies

Most of Myanmar’s manganese mines have been running since the early 2000s in Shan State.

The NDAA, backed by the United Wa State Party and with deep ties to China, used those connections to become a powerhouse in rare earth and jade mining.
